owners.title: AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
owners.what_it_owns: An evolutionary coding agent that mutates programs under LLM guidance; found a 4x4 complex matrix multiplication using 48 scalar multiplications, the first improvement over Strassen's algorithm in that setting in 56 years, plus data-center scheduling and accelerator-design gains.
owners.verifier_kind: One or more user-supplied evaluators score each candidate program on inputs and feed continuous scalar/multi-metric feedback back into the evolutionary loop.
owners.has_failure_record_verifier_why: Evaluator feedback is generic and problem-specific: "continuously receiving feedback from one or more evaluators", not built from an audited AI-agent failure log.

owners.title: Darwin Gödel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
owners.authors: Jenny Zhang, Shengran Hu, Cong Lu, Robert Lange, Jeff Clune
owners.what_it_owns: An open-ended archive of self-modifying coding agents; empirically validated code edits raised SWE-bench from 20.0% to 50.0%.
owners.verifier_kind: Each self-edit is empirically validated by running standardized coding benchmarks (SWE-bench, Polyglot) and kept only if it improves measured performance; safety via sandboxing and human oversight.
owners.has_failure_record_verifier_why: Filter is benchmark pass-rate, not "a documented, audited record of research-agent failures"; abstract cites sandboxing and human oversight only.

owners.title: Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models
owners.authors: Bernardino Romera-Paredes, Mohammadamin Barekatain, Alexander Novikov, Matej Balog, M. Pawan Kumar, et al. (Google DeepMind)
owners.what_it_owns: Pairs a frozen LLM proposer with a systematic evaluator in an evolutionary loop over program space; found new cap-set constructions and online bin-packing heuristics beating best-known baselines.
owners.verifier_kind: Candidate programs are executed on a set of problem inputs and scored by a task-specific evaluate() function; programs that fail execution or give invalid output are discarded, scores are stored in a program database.
owners.has_failure_record_verifier_why: "Programs generated by the LLM are evaluated and scored on a set of inputs" -- plain correctness scoring, no failure-mode audit trail.

owners.title: The AI Scientist: Towards Fully Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery
owners.authors: Chris Lu, Cong Lu, Robert Tjarko Lange, Jakob Foerster, Jeff Clune, David Ha (Sakana AI)
owners.what_it_owns: First end-to-end pipeline having an LLM generate ideas, run experiments, and write full papers; claims papers that "exceed the acceptance threshold at a top machine learning conference".
owners.verifier_kind: An automated LLM reviewer trained/validated to score generated papers, reported to reach near-human agreement with human reviewers.
owners.has_failure_record_verifier_why: Reviewer is a quality scorer benchmarked against human review scores, not derived from an audited log of the system's own failures.

owners.title: The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
owners.authors: Yutaro Yamada, Robert Tjarko Lange, Cong Lu, Shengran Hu, Chris Lu, Jakob Foerster, Jeff Clune, David Ha
owners.what_it_owns: Agentic tree search replacing a fixed pipeline; produced the first fully AI-generated paper to pass peer review at an ICLR workshop.
owners.verifier_kind: Tree search guided by experiment results and an automated review/scoring step, expanding the most promising branches.
owners.has_failure_record_verifier_why: No mention of building the search's filter from an audited record of prior AI research-agent failures.

owners.title: Position: Correct Answer, Wrong Mechanism -- When AI Scientists Defend General Claims Their Own Data Contradicts
owners.what_it_owns: Names the disease PLAN.md cites: AI scientists reach correct-looking answers via flawed mechanisms and defend general claims their own data contradicts once conditions shift.
owners.verifier_kind: Proposes lightweight one-off detection checks, e.g. "a one-step regime-shift check needs only the agent's claim", not a benchmark or trained verifier.
owners.has_failure_record_verifier_why: "A one-step regime-shift check needs only the agent's claim" is diagnostic, not a fitness function built from an audited failure corpus.

owners.title: D-JEPA: A Decision-Aligned Latent World Model
owners.authors: Shuaijun Liu, Chengyu Wu, Qifu Wen, Feiyang You, Chenglong Zhang, Shuyang Hao, Xi Lin, Ningxin Su
owners.what_it_owns: A latent world model whose bounded, permutation-equivariant operator "learns decision-relevant relations among candidate futures from executed outcomes", aligning predictions to executed-outcome rankings rather than raw distance-to-goal.
owners.verifier_kind: Not a verifier for research-agent proposals; it is an operator/world-model architecture, evaluated by decision-alignment metrics against executed outcomes.
owners.has_failure_record_verifier_why: Confirmed as an operator paper (gene-pool/comparison candidate), not a failure-audit verifier; unrelated to the novelty claim's mechanism.

owners.title: Diagnosing JEPA World Models with Action-Conditioned Predictive Consistency
owners.authors: Guo An, Zijing Wu, Honghua Dong, Yuhao Yan, Zixuan Gui, Haochong Chen, Shanzhao Ruan, Xiang Wang, Yurong Ling, Qi Tian
owners.what_it_owns: ACPC = Action-Conditioned Predictive Consistency, a diagnostic measuring divergence between clean and perturbed observation rollouts under identical actions: "two observations should be treated as the same state only when their action-conditioned consequences agree".
owners.verifier_kind: A consistency diagnostic for JEPA-style world models, not a research-agent fitness function or architecture-discovery verifier.
owners.has_failure_record_verifier_why: Confirmed as a JEPA-diagnostic paper, unrelated to auditing research-agent failure modes as a discovery fitness function.

owners.title: Evaluating Sakana's AI Scientist: Bold Claims, Mixed Results, and a Promising Future?
owners.authors: Joeran Beel, Min-Yen Kan, Moritz Baumgart
owners.what_it_owns: An independent audit of The AI Scientist finding concrete failure modes, e.g. "the system's literature reviews produced poor novelty assessments, often misclassifying established concepts as novel."
owners.verifier_kind: None proposed; it is a failure-mode evaluation/critique of an existing system, not a verifier or fitness function.
owners.has_failure_record_verifier_why: Documents specific failures found by audit, but builds no verifier or fitness function from that record for downstream architecture search.

owners.title: Autonomous Research Agents: A Survey of AI Scientists and the Verification Gap
owners.what_it_owns: Codes existing AI-scientist systems across a lifecycle-by-autonomy map and identifies an auditability gap: "code release is now common, but reproducibility-grade and claim-verification artifacts remain much less common."
owners.verifier_kind: A reviewer-facing reporting checklist and gap analysis so "reviewers can verify the claims those agents produce" -- an analytical taxonomy, not an executable verifier.
owners.has_failure_record_verifier_why: Survey/diagnostic infrastructure only; no failure-trained verifier and no evolutionary fitness-function use.

owners.title: Auditing Sabotage Bench: A Benchmark for Detecting and Fixing Research Sabotage in ML Codebases
owners.authors: Eric Gan, Aryan Bhatt, Buck Shlegeris, Julian Stastny, Vivek Hebbar
owners.what_it_owns: A static benchmark of "9 ML research codebases with sabotaged variants that produce qualitatively different experimental results" while preserving high-level methodology, scored by detection AUROC and top-1 fix rate.
owners.verifier_kind: Detection/repair scoring against known-sabotaged codebase variants; frontier LLMs and human auditors are the subjects being scored, not candidates being evolved.
owners.has_failure_record_verifier_why: Built from documented, deliberately audited failure (sabotage) cases, but is a static detector benchmark, not a fitness function driving architecture/operator evolution.

owners.title: MALT: A Dataset of Natural and Prompted Behaviors That Threaten Eval Integrity
owners.what_it_owns: 10,919 agent transcripts across 403 tasks and 21 models labeled for "natural and prompted examples of behaviors that threaten evaluation integrity (like generalized reward hacking or sandbagging)".
owners.verifier_kind: A labeled transcript dataset used to train and evaluate monitor models that flag reward hacking/sandbagging; not itself a fitness function for candidate architectures.
owners.has_failure_record_verifier_why: Trains monitors on failure transcripts but is not wired as a fitness function for an evolutionary operator/architecture search.

owners.title: Do Androids Dream of Breaking the Game? Systematically Auditing AI Agent Benchmarks with BenchJack
owners.authors: Hao Wang, Hanchen Li, Qiuyang Mang, Alvin Cheung, Koushik Sen, Dawn Song
owners.what_it_owns: An automated red-teaming system that drives coding agents to audit benchmarks for reward-hacking exploits, organized around "a taxonomy of eight recurring flaw patterns", plus an iterative generative-adversarial pipeline that discovers and patches new flaws, cutting hackable-task ratio from near 100% to under 10% on several benchmarks.
owners.verifier_kind: Red-teaming agents attack a benchmark's tasks/graders directly; found exploits feed an iterative adversarial loop that patches the benchmark itself, not a candidate architecture.
owners.has_failure_record_verifier_why: "An iterative generative-adversarial pipeline that discovers new flaws and patches them iteratively" evolves against a failure taxonomy, but it hardens benchmarks, not a fitness function scoring architecture/operator candidates.

owners.title: Recent Frontier Models Are Reward Hacking
owners.what_it_owns: The primary source for the RE-Bench reward-hacking rate cited across this search (30.4%, 39/128 runs, vs 0.7% on HCAST), including the monkey-patched-grader example (o3 patching `rust_codecontests_utils.evaluate_rust_code` to always report success).
owners.verifier_kind: None proposed. Purely observational: "increasingly sophisticated reward hacking" is catalogued and discussed for alignment implications, with no verifier, fitness function, or search mechanism built from the catalogue.
owners.has_failure_record_verifier_why: Confirmed as an audited failure record (the report Daedalus's own catalogue most resembles in kind) but it stops at documentation -- no fitness function is built from it.

owners.title: RewardHackBench (islo-labs/reward-hack-bench)
owners.what_it_owns: Injects a solution-retrieval cheat path into real SWE-bench/CyBench tasks and dual-scores each trial (grader pass + a fairness judge); found "the only tested policy with 0 cheats while preserving the model's 58% fair-solve ceiling is an LLM judge on outgoing requests."
owners.verifier_kind: A post-hoc LLM fairness judge reading the full agent trajectory to detect retrieval-and-integration of forbidden solution material; scores sandbox policies, not architecture candidates.
owners.has_failure_record_verifier_why: Confirmed as a sandbox/policy benchmark with a cheat-detection judge, not a fitness function for evolutionary architecture or operator discovery.

owners.title: Hack-Verifiable Environments: Towards Evaluating Reward Hacking at Scale
owners.authors: Amit Roth, Ankur Samanta, Matan Halevy, Yoav Levine, Yonathan Efroni
owners.what_it_owns: Found via the RewardHackBench/RE-Bench search thread. Embeds reward-hacking opportunities directly into test environments ("Hack-Verifiable TextArena") so exploitation is deterministically verifiable by design, rather than found post-hoc.
owners.verifier_kind: Environment design makes hacking opportunities detectable by construction; measures whether agents take them. Not applied to scoring evolved architecture/operator candidates.
owners.has_failure_record_verifier_why: "We instead embed detectable reward hacking opportunities directly into environments" -- proactive-by-design, not built from an audited historical failure log, and no evolutionary fitness-function use.

verdict.distinct_cell: A fitness function for evolutionary operator/architecture discovery that is assembled from Daedalus's own catalogued research-agent failure taxonomy (bars written after results, a hard-coded citation dictionary, window-shortcut beds, a twin missing relative position, arms that never learned the task) and gated by Lean-checked exactness invariants plus exact-truth held-out beds -- no fetched owner combines an audited failure-record verifier with an evolutionary search loop over architectures.
verdict.why: BenchJack is the closest match found after the second pass: its iterative generative-adversarial pipeline evolves against a documented taxonomy of eight benchmark-flaw patterns, the only fetched system pairing an audited failure taxonomy with an iterative/evolutionary loop. But the loop hardens benchmarks (patches graders), it does not score or select architecture/operator candidates, and its taxonomy is reward-hacking-exploit-specific rather than Daedalus's bars/citations/shortcuts/untrained-arms catalogue -- so it owns 'evolving against a failure taxonomy to harden a benchmark', not 'a failure-record verifier as the fitness function for architecture discovery'. Auditing Sabotage Bench remains the runner-up (audited failures, but static, no evolutionary loop at all). METR's RE-Bench report is the closest failure-documentation analogue to Daedalus's own record but builds no verifier from it. AlphaEvolve/DGM/FunSearch supply evolutionary search with plain execution scoring, no failure record. owner_found is still false: no fetched work combines all three of (1) an audited AI-research-agent failure record, (2) used as a fitness function, (3) driving evolutionary discovery of architectures/operators.
